title: A Condor Flew 100 Miles Without Flapping Its Wings Once

scenes.text: A condor flew over a hundred miles without flapping once.
That's about five hours in the air, on ten-foot wings, with zero wingbeats.
Scientists tracked eight condors for more than 250 hours.
They flapped only about one percent of that time.
Most of the flapping was just taking off.
In the air, they ride rising warm air and wind instead of burning energy.
So yes: a hundred miles, not one flap.

description:
A condor flew over a hundred miles without flapping once.
Researchers tracked eight Andean condors for more than 250 hours and found they flap about one percent of the time.
Would you rather soar like a condor or swim like a seal?
first_comment: Bonus: a condor weighs about 33 pounds. How does something that heavy stay up with no effort?
